stem: A gaming company runs game servers on Amazon EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Players worldwide connect to these servers. The same instances also serve large game patch files to players over HTTPS through the load balancers. Every player downloads the same files, and the files change once a week. The company wants to reduce the download time of the patch files for players who are far from both Regions. Which solution will provide the LOWEST latency for these downloads?
keywords: serve large game patch files to players over HTTPS
the files change once a week

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the two Network Load Balancers as origins, and point the game client at the domain name of the distribution.
options.why: Patch files are content that [benefits from edge delivery](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-good-for-static-edge-content): edge locations keep copies, so most downloads are answered close to the players.

options.text: Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator with one listener and an endpoint group for the Network Load Balancer in each of the two Regions.
options.why: It works for HTTPS, but it improves performance by [proxying packets at the edge](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-vs-cloudfront-content-types), so every download still reaches the instances and nothing is cached.

options.text: Create Amazon Route 53 latency-based records that point to the two Network Load Balancers, and point the game client at the name of the records.
options.why: It works, but Route 53 only answers with the record whose [Region gives the user the lowest latency](../facts/route53.md#route53-latency-routing-lowest-latency-region); every download still comes from the instances in that Region.

options.text: Turn on Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration for a bucket that stores the game data, and point the game client at the accelerated endpoint of the bucket.
options.why: Transfer Acceleration routes data to and from a bucket [over an optimized network path](../facts/s3.md#s3-transfer-acceleration-how-it-works), and it keeps no cached copies near the players.
options.misconception: S3 Transfer Acceleration caches content at edge locations

explanation: Patch files change once a week, so copies can stay at the edge. CloudFront suits [frequently accessed static content](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-good-for-static-edge-content) such as software downloads. Each request goes to the [edge location that provides the lowest latency](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-request-routed-lowest-latency-edge), where a cached copy answers it without a trip to either Region.
takeaway: Large files that many users download: CloudFront caches them at the edge; Global Accelerator does not cache.
twin: If the stem said "Players send their moves over UDP, and partner networks must allow-list a fixed set of IP addresses" instead: Global Accelerator, because it supports [both TCP and UDP protocols](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-protocols-tcp-and-udp) from fixed addresses.
say: Patch files are cacheable, so CloudFront serves them from edge locations near the players.
